name: Revenue Growth Quality
trigger: Revenue is rising, but profit is falling
explanation: Revenue is growing, but profit is contracting. This indicates the business is growing inefficiently, taking on low-margin work or allowing expenses to run out of control.
action: Review the pricing models for new orders and audit the core cost of goods sold.

name: Expense Pressure
trigger: Expense growth exceeds revenue growth rate
explanation: Outflow growth is outpacing top-line growth, narrowing operating cushions.
action: Implement a department-by-department expense budget ceiling.

name: Cash Runway Warning
trigger: Cash runway is less than 90 days
explanation: The business represents severe insolvency risk if trading conditions worsen.
action: Accelerate outstanding receivables collections and freeze all non-essential operating spend.

name: Customer Concentration Risk
trigger: Single customer represents > 35% of total revenue
explanation: High dependency on a single customer makes the business extremely volatile to customer churn.
action: Proactively pitch and identify replacement prospects to reduce single-customer share below 35%.

name: Vendor Concentration Risk
trigger: Single vendor represents > 30% of total expenses
explanation: High dependency on a single vendor leaves the firm open to pricing monopolies or supply disruption.
action: Identify and qualify alternative suppliers or negotiate long-term price locks.

name: Margin Compression
trigger: Gross margin decreases continuously for 3 periods
explanation: Continuous erosion of margins implies cost of goods sold is inflating faster than primary selling prices.
action: Hike sales pricing immediately or select alternative lower-cost suppliers.

name: Payroll Drift
trigger: Payroll increases > 20% without equivalent revenue growth support
explanation: The head count expense is rising much faster than the sales capacity it should serve.
action: Audit employee utilization and optimize staff schedules before opening new hires.

name: Marketing Efficiency Slump
trigger: Marketing expenses rise strongly while revenue remains flat
explanation: The marginal Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) is spiking, reflecting saturated advertising channels.
action: Pause underperforming ad sets and run a deep review of marketing attribution model.

name: Inventory Buildup
trigger: Inventory assets rise faster than monthly sales growth
explanation: Working capital is getting locked up in unsold warehouse stock, threatening liquidity.
action: Introduce markdown pricing to flush stale inventory and freeze active production items.

name: Receivable Collections Stress
trigger: Customer payment days (DSO) lengthening over 45 days
explanation: Customers are taking longer to pay, which acts as an informal interests-free loan and starves company cash.
action: Establish strict upfront milestones and implement automatic late payment interests.

name: Payable Stress
trigger: Supplier payment days lengthening sharply
explanation: Lengthening payments to suppliers can signal liquidity squeeze and harm supplier trust.
action: Review payment terms and ensure active dynamic discounting is utilized where possible.

name: Period-End Clustered Entries
trigger: Large transactions representing > 40% of monthly values clustered at month-end
explanation: Massive adjustments clustered at month-end might suggest poor billing practices or artificial revenue recognition in current periods.
action: Enforce weekly transaction classification and reconcile invoice billing batches strictly.

name: Duplicate Payments Detected
trigger: Multiple transactions with identical amounts, dates, and vendors
explanation: Identical supplier payments indicates weak internal double-match controls or potential billing errors.
action: Verify invoice item IDs, contact the vendor to arrange charge credit, and upgrade accounts payable software.

name: Round-Number Spikes
trigger: Unusual volume of exact thousands or flat transaction amounts
explanation: Substantial quantity of flat numbers represents higher risk of manually inflated expense requests or un-receipted entries.
action: Mandate exact receipt attachment for any manual journal ledger entries.

name: Reversal Postings Pattern
trigger: Large journal reversals posted immediately after period closures
explanation: P&L inflating adjustments posted at period end and reversed immediately after might imply window dressing of accounts.
action: Audit the credentials of characters releasing adjustments within the ERP.

name: Extreme Revenue Volatility
trigger: Month-to-month sales fluctuation exceeds 30%
explanation: Wild swings in core revenues make operational scaling and fixed-expense management incredibly difficult.
action: Formulate a dry-season cash buffer equal to 4 months of median operating costs.

name: Customer Contribution Shift
trigger: Aggressive shifts in customer contribution share in top 5 slots
explanation: Key client base contribution structures are rapidly changing, indicating customer churn or contract resizing.
action: Initiate structured account health check-ins with client managers.

name: Vendor Price Inflation
trigger: Supplier materials price index rising faster than overall margin
explanation: Squeezes bottom-line margins continuously as suppliers inflate utility pricing.
action: Conduct competitive bidding among alternative logistics and material service vendors.

name: Debt Service Coverage Warning
trigger: Operating cash flow is lower than quarterly debt servicing obligations
explanation: Operating cash is insufficient to pay interests, requiring drawing on primary reserve balances.
action: Renegotiate current bank interest rate structures or seek mezzanine loan refinancing.

name: Slowing Sales Run-Rate
trigger: Current period sales are > 25% lower than the rolling 3-period average
explanation: Sharp collapse in demand which will quickly affect overall survival metric and cause fixed-cost strains.
action: Incentivize long-term contract conversions or launch defensive volume discounts.
